queue.title: As US credit card debt hits $1.29T, bank algorithms are rejecting debt-free, six-figure earners
queue.dek: Across the country, debt-free Americans earning six figures face credit card denials as bank algorithms flag thin credit files as high-risk behavior.
queue.opening: Across the country, Americans earning six-figure salaries, carrying no debt and sitting on healthy savings accounts are increasingly hitting an unexpected wall when applying for everyday credit cards or loans: instant denial from automated bank algorithms. The rejections highlight a growing rift between kitchen-table financial discipline and corporate underwriting models. While nationwide credit card balances have climbed to a record $1.29 trillion — a 67% surge since early 2021, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York — data from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) shows an estimated 25 million adults have credit files "too thin" or stale to generate a standard score. Rather than rewarding households that avoid borrowing, modern underwriting algorithms can interpret limited recent credit activity as a sign of uncertain lending risk, potentially making it harder for some debt-free consumers to qualify for credit. "Is corporate America penalizing people who live debt-free? I would say they're not penalizing them, but they are not prioritizing them because we're not the ones making them money," Jade Warshaw, co-host of "The Ramsey Show" — who paid off $460,000 in debt alongside her husband — told Fox News Digital. "When you think about the credit score in general, the whole purpose, it's a product, and so it's out there for banks to make money. queue.dek: A Northwestern Medicine study found that marijuana users had objectively worse sleep quality, even though they didn't perceive their sleep as worse. Other experts weighed in.
queue.opening: Marijuana may be making sleep quality worse, despite its widespread use as a sleep aid, a recent Northwestern Medicine study found. The findings of the study , which included 1,266 participants, showed that both lifetime and recent cannabis users objectively had worse sleep quality, although they did not report their sleep to be worse. Participants were monitored for almost 35 years, from young adulthood into middle age, with scientists tracking their use of cannabis over time. AMERICA HITS MAJOR MARIJUANA MILESTONE AS DAILY WEED USE SURPASSES DAILY DRINKING In middle age, participants wore a sleep monitor on their wrist for a week and filled out surveys about their sleep quality . This allowed researchers to compare objective and subjective reports of participants’ sleep. "Our data do not support the belief that cannabis is helpful as a sleep aid," said senior study author Mercedes R. Carnethon, Ph.D., as Northwestern Now reported. "As cannabis becomes increasingly available and accepted, it's important to better understand its long-term associations with health behaviors such as sleep," Carnethon added. queue.opening: Elon Musk's SpaceX made history Saturday after its Starship spacecraft returned from orbit and was caught by giant mechanical arms at the company's Texas launch facility for the first time. The milestone came roughly 22 hours after Starship launched Friday from SpaceX's Starbase facility, although the company fell short of its goal of recovering both stages of the rocket after its Super Heavy booster exploded over the Gulf of America. The catch marks a major step toward SpaceX's goal of developing a fully reusable rocket system to reduce launch costs and support more frequent space missions. Walter Isaacson, Musk's biographer, celebrated the achievement on X, recalling a December 2020 meeting when Musk proposed catching Starship with the launch tower's mechanical arms. "This is actually a bigger deal for humanity than most people can imagine," he wrote. "I will always remember the looks on the engineers’ faces in the Starbase conference room in December 2020 when @elonmusk suggested, then insisted, that the Mechazilla launchpad arms could catch a returning Starship." Some winners are casting the results as a mandate to challenge President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown and putting prospective 2028 Democratic presidential candidates on notice.
